clusters.label: Chemical stability
clusters.definition: Persistence of chemical integrity against chemical change or decomposition.
clusters.reason: All denote chemical stability as a material property. Energetic calculations, bonding arguments and kinetic restrictions provide different grounds for that property; their mechanisms and claim qualifications remain separate.

clusters.label: Flexible electronics
clusters.definition: Electronic applications using mechanically flexible materials or devices.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly identify the same application field; the proposed materials and devices remain distinct.

clusters.label: Carbon nanotubes
clusters.definition: The material class of tubular carbon nanostructures.
clusters.reason: Both labels genuinely denote carbon nanotubes without conflicting composition or subtype qualifiers. Electrode and photothermoelectric roles do not change the material class.

clusters.label: High flexibility
clusters.definition: A pronounced ability of a device to undergo mechanical bending or deformation.
clusters.reason: Both describe the same qualitative mechanical property, without specifying different flexibility mechanisms or quantitative criteria.

clusters.label: Electronic thermal conductivity
clusters.definition: The contribution of electronic carriers to thermal conductivity in the studied samples.
clusters.reason: Both denote the electronic heat-transport quantity reduced following doping, rather than the reduction itself.

clusters.label: Electronic thermal conductivity (predicted)
clusters.definition: Electronic-carrier thermal conductivity evaluated within a DFT and semiclassical Boltzmann transport framework.
clusters.reason: The supplied context explicitly identifies a theoretical prediction, retained separately from sample-based conductivity reports.

clusters.label: Electron effective mass
clusters.definition: The effective mass of electrons associated with transport in the chromium-doped material.
clusters.reason: The evidence concerns the electron effective mass maintained or enhanced in a doped sample; the enhancement is a separate claim.

clusters.label: Electron effective mass (DFT)
clusters.definition: Electron effective mass in the DFT description of Dy2CoMnO6.
clusters.reason: Explicitly a theoretical electronic-structure quantity, distinguished from the sample-based report and from hole effective mass.

clusters.label: ZT
clusters.definition: The dimensionless thermoelectric figure of merit.
clusters.reason: All denote the same thermoelectric performance quantity. Capitalization, material, temperature, maximum values and directions of change belong to the individual claims.

clusters.label: Cubic structure
clusters.definition: Crystal structure belonging to the cubic crystal system.
clusters.reason: Each label denotes cubic structural symmetry, without asserting that the compounds have identical atomic structures or are the same material.

clusters.label: Semiconducting nature
clusters.definition: Semiconducting electronic character without a specified direct or indirect gap subtype.
clusters.reason: These mentions establish semiconducting character without specifying a shared narrower gap subtype. The parent-material and trigonal-phase qualifiers remain attached to their claims.

clusters.label: Semiconducting nature (indirect gap)
clusters.definition: Semiconducting electronic character with an indirect band gap.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly attribute semiconducting behavior to indirect band gaps; material identities and gap values remain distinct.

clusters.label: Semiconducting nature (spin-resolved direct gaps)
clusters.definition: Semiconducting character with direct gaps specified separately for spin-up and spin-down states.
clusters.reason: The evidence explicitly supplies direct, spin-dependent gaps, a narrower electronic subtype than the other mentions.

clusters.label: Total thermal conductivity
clusters.definition: Overall thermal conductivity including the contributing heat-transport channels.
clusters.reason: These sample-based reports denote the same total heat-transport quantity. Increases, decreases, mechanisms and numerical values remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Total thermal conductivity (predicted)
clusters.definition: Overall thermal conductivity evaluated in a DFT and semiclassical Boltzmann transport study.
clusters.reason: The theoretical prediction is explicitly distinguished from sample-based thermal-conductivity reports.

clusters.label: Ionic character
clusters.definition: Ionic character of bonding or constituent atoms in a material.
clusters.reason: All describe ionic bonding character, supported by explicit ionic-material, bond, charge-density or related descriptions. Species, dimensionality, inference methods and composition-dependent decreases remain in their claims.

clusters.label: Ionic character (interfacial bonds)
clusters.definition: The ionic component of newly formed chemical bonds at the Cu3Sn/Cu interface.
clusters.reason: Explicitly concerns interfacial bonding, with coexisting covalent character, and is kept distinct from material-level ionic character.

clusters.label: Charge-carrier scattering (optical phonons)
clusters.definition: Scattering of charge carriers by strongly coupled optical phonon modes in the studied monolayers.
clusters.reason: The evidence explicitly identifies optical phonons as the dominant scattering mechanism.

clusters.label: Charge-carrier scattering (nanoscale porosity)
clusters.definition: Scattering of charge carriers promoted by nanoscale porosity in bulk La-doped SrTiO3.
clusters.reason: The evidence attributes scattering to introduced porosity, a distinct mechanism and bulk context.

clusters.label: Glass substrate
clusters.definition: A glass support on which a film or device is fabricated.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly denote the same substrate material class; no specific glass composition or identical physical substrate is asserted.

clusters.label: Energy harvesting
clusters.definition: Collection and conversion of available energy into usable energy.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly name the general application, without defining incompatible narrower harvesting processes.

clusters.label: Orthorhombic phase
clusters.definition: A crystalline phase exhibiting orthorhombic symmetry.
clusters.reason: Both denote orthorhombic structural symmetry. The distinct compositions, phase conditions and octahedral distortion remain attached to their respective claims.
